scope: Untrained shared business-environment diagnostic; not a pure SAC or EQN training result.
units: Original exported numerical units; currency and price scaling not independently verified.

memory_mutation.explanation: Changing only previous_price/previous_response does not affect response or dynamics for the same new action and RNG state.

full19_redundancies.note: Gross load and forecasts are recoverable from current net_load, wind and hour up to float32 rounding. Price/wind history can still convey extra information in three-source stochastic cases.

boundary_summary.note: 121-point deterministic one-hour profit scan with storage off; not a trained policy or proof for all scenarios.

peak_penalty_tradeoff.objective: Operating cost + coefficient * daily maximum grid purchase; offline fixed-price diagnostic only.
peak_penalty_tradeoff.coefficient_units: Original unverified monetary units per unit of daily peak power; not a calibrated tariff recommendation.

separable_candidate_changes.name: compact11_observation_only
separable_candidate_changes.scope: Controlled follow-up to the unchanged full19 SAC baseline; leave reward and physical parameters unchanged.
separable_candidate_changes.rationale: Fixed hourly temperature, three equal previous-price slots, unused previous response and three algebraically recoverable forecasts are redundant under the current environment assumptions. Explicit forecast features may still help optimization, so this is an ablation candidate rather than a proven improvement.

separable_candidate_changes.name: explicit_peak_objective_if_peak_shaving_is_required
separable_candidate_changes.proposal: Augment observations with running peak; apply penalty coefficient * (new_running_peak - old_running_peak). The sum equals coefficient * daily peak when initialized at zero.
separable_candidate_changes.scope: Independent objective change, not part of a pure-profit baseline. Calibrate the unit and operational tradeoff before selecting a coefficient.

separable_candidate_changes.name: separate_price_curtailment_from_energy_shifting
separable_candidate_changes.proposal: Current demand response is per-hour curtailment/increase with no backlog or rebound. If a deferrable-load interpretation is required, implement energy balance/backlog and deadline state in a separate environment version.

separable_candidate_changes.name: preserve_physical_data_and_clarify_terminal_scope
separable_candidate_changes.proposal: Do not change capacity, efficiency, initial SOC or price units to improve a 500-episode curve. Initial usable energy is zero. Free final SOC models a one-day problem; continuous operation would require explicit carry-over or a justified terminal value in another environment version.

proposed_fixed_target_shape_penalty.formula: weight * mean_nominal_grid_price * max_load * ((grid_purchase - target) / max_load)^2 per hour
proposed_fixed_target_shape_penalty.information_boundary: Target uses known nominal profile and configured expected wind penetration; no future realized data is used.

calibration_relative_to_fixed_mid_price_.warning: Matching the penalty scale to a 5%/10% profit budget is an initialization heuristic, not a guarantee on realized profit loss. Validate actual paired economic performance on held-out seeds.

traps: The squared penalty equals variance plus squared mean bias around a fixed target. It rewards raising an economical low mean through demand increases or charging, not only shaving high peaks.
The nominal target ignores price-induced demand changes; different price policies have different daily net energy. Wind reference realization also differs from expected 20% penetration.
Unused terminal energy can reduce the shape penalty while losing cash. Audit final usable SOC and charging in the final hours separately.
An L2 tracking penalty does not directly constrain the maximum grid purchase or ramps. Always report peak, valley, standard deviation and max ramp in addition to shaped reward.
Coefficient units depend on original unverified price/power units. This is an operational preference regularizer, not an identified demand-charge tariff.
